title: Ship defensive CSS for dynamic content
principle: Ahmad Shadeed’s Defensive CSS (ishadeed.com → defensivecss.dev): write CSS that survives unexpected content—long titles, odd image ratios, extra flex items—instead of styling only the happy-path mock. For AI UI work, treat every generated layout as hostile until proven robust.
procedure: List failure modes: overflow text, missing images, 1 vs 12 items, RTL, zoom.
For each component, add a defensive rule (wrap, min/max, object-fit, gap, line-clamp with escape).
Prefer flex-wrap / auto-fit patterns over fixed counts assumed by the mock.
Add CSS variable fallbacks where tokens may be missing.
QA with ugly content fixtures, not lorem-perfect strings.
examplePrompts:
Apply Defensive CSS (Shadeed / defensivecss.dev) to this component set:
- Long titles must wrap or truncate without breaking siblings.
- Images: object-fit + fixed aspect so distortion can’t wreck the card.
- Flex/grid: wrap or scroll when item count exceeds the mock.
- Provide CSS variable fallbacks.
Return before/after snippets + the failure mode each fix covers.
Generate three hostile content fixtures (emoji-heavy title, 2KB bio, 0.5× image) and harden the CSS until the layout holds.
promptWhy: Names concrete failure modes so the model doesn’t ‘prettify’ only the screenshot case.
Fixtures force proof—AI often claims robustness without testing.
tips: Built on Shadeed’s earlier ‘just in case’ mindset essays.
Quiet Folio: defense is craft, not chrome.

workedExamples.title: Card title nuke
workedExamples.before: One-line title; AI CSS uses nowrap + fixed height—long titles collide.
workedExamples.after: Wrap with line-clamp(2) + min-height; siblings use gap not absolute offsets.
workedExamples.body: Classic defensive tip: plan for long content.

workedExamples.title: Flex row of ‘exactly 4’
workedExamples.before: Four equal columns; fifth item from CMS overflows off-screen.
workedExamples.after: flex-wrap + min widths; or horizontal scroll with visible cue.

workedExamples.title: Broken hero image
workedExamples.body: Unexpected aspect ratio: lock box with aspect-ratio + object-fit:cover so layout geometry stays.

antiPatterns: Styling only the Figma-perfect string lengths.
Fixed pixel heights that clip real copy.
Assuming image dimensions match the mock forever.

provenance.statement: Design Catalog editorial synthesis of the cited public sources; contracts and decision paths are our implementation guidance, not quotations or author endorsements.

useWhen: Does the same task survive narrow screens and longer content?
avoidWhen: Do not fix one screenshot with a fixed height or a device-specific offset.
inputs: A concrete user problem and the current artifact
Constraints, existing behavior and source attribution to preserve
agentContract.output: A bounded application of “Ship defensive CSS for dynamic content” with before/after evidence and remaining limitations.
acceptance: At 320px, 390px and 1280px, and at 200% zoom, long titles wrap; controls remain reachable; only intrinsically wide content scrolls horizontally.

stateRequirements.responsive: Check 390px and desktop plus 200% zoom; preserve reading order, wrap long text and keep actions reachable.
stateRequirements.accessibility: Use semantic headings and native controls, visible labels and focus; normal text contrast at least 4.5:1.
stateRequirements.keyboard: Complete the primary action using Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter and Space; no pointer-only information or focus trap.
stateRequirements.reducedMotion: Remove nonessential movement; preserve all state and information without waiting for animation.
stateRequirements.loading: Show pending feedback only during real work; retain context and allow navigation away.
stateRequirements.empty: Distinguish no content from no matching results; explain how to proceed or reset filters.
stateRequirements.error: Explain the failed action, retain user input and offer recovery; never claim success on failure.
stateRequirements.interruption: A newer action wins; cancel or ignore stale results and keep controls responsive.
stateRequirements.stateChange: Announce important results politely without moving focus unexpectedly.

compatibility.rule: Start with one technique. Add at most one companion for a distinct unsolved problem; candidates are suggestions, not verified compatibility.
conflicts: Two techniques changing the same visual role require an explicit winner.
Do not combine multiple entrance or attention effects on one target.
Aesthetic subtraction must not remove semantics, feedback or attribution.
compatibility.stop: Content reflows without hiding essential actions or changing reading order.

comparison.bad: A fixed three-column grid clips labels and pushes the final action off screen.
comparison.good: A content-sized grid stacks in source order and lets long labels wrap.
comparison.impact: Content reflows without hiding essential actions or changing reading order.
